name: Maddur Vada
instructions: 1. In a large bowl, mix rice flour, semolina, maida, salt, cumin seeds, and asafoetida.
2. Add chopped onions, green chilies, and curry leaves to the flour mixture.
3. Pour 2 tablespoons of hot oil over the mixture and rub it in well.
4. Gradually add very little water to form a firm, non-sticky dough.
5. Heat oil in a deep pan for frying.
6. Take a small portion of the dough, flatten it into a thick disc using your palm, and carefully slide it into the hot oil.
7. Deep fry on medium heat until both sides are golden brown and crispy.
8. Remove and drain on paper towels before serving hot.
description: Maddur Vada is a famous deep-fried snack originating from the town of Maddur in Karnataka, located on the Bangalore-Mysore railway line. It is traditionally sold by vendors at the Maddur railway station and is cherished for its signature crunchy texture and the sweetness of caramelized onions.
